# Outreach plan, week of 2 March 2026

## 1. Mary Major, VP Operations, Harborline Distribution

**Email 1 (Day 0)**
**Subject:** Your Stackwise question, and sorry for the slow answer

Hi Mary,

You asked in our webinar Q&A whether Ironbark Sense works with Stackwise. Nobody replied, and that's our miss. I'm sorry.

Here is the straight answer. We do have a Stackwise integration, but it's API-based and still in **beta**, with about three customers live. It isn't yet generally available like our other two WMS integrations.

Whether beta is good enough depends on what you need Stackwise and Sense to share across your three DCs. If you tell me, I'll give you an honest view of whether it fits today. I can also bring a colleague from our integrations side.

Do you have 20 minutes this week or next?

Best,
[Name], Ironbark Safety

*(~140 words)*

**Email 2 (Day 3)**
**Subject:** What a 38-truck DC saw in six months

Hi Mary,

Here is the evidence behind the webinar. At Coldbrook Foods, one DC with 38 forklifts, recorded near-miss events fell **60% over six months**. Forklift impacts went from 9 to 4 in the first 12 months. That is one site's result, not a promise for yours.

Harborline is larger, so I'd test it before committing. Our pilot runs 30 days on up to 10 trucks at one site, at no charge. We can include the Stackwise beta in the pilot or leave it out. That's your call, and it lets you judge the integration on your own data.

If you tell me which DC and roughly which 10 trucks you'd choose, I'll draft a one-page pilot plan for you to react to.

Best,
[Name]

*(~140 words)*

**Email 3 (Day 8)**
**Subject:** 200 new hires and a fourth DC

Hi Mary,

I saw the news that Harborline has leased a fourth DC in Reno and plans to hire about 200 warehouse staff by summer. Congratulations.

A hiring wave like that puts a lot of new people on the floor around trucks. Sense is built for that: proximity alerts when trucks and pedestrians get close, impact detection, and operator check-in. Pricing starts at $45 per vehicle per month, so 10 trucks at the starting rate is $450 a month.

A practical sequence would be to run the free 30-day pilot at an existing DC now. By the time Reno opens, you'd know what works and what your Stackwise needs are.

Would 20 minutes next week work to map that out? If the timing is wrong, tell me and I'll check back later.

Best,
[Name]

*(~150 words)*

---

## 2. John Stiles, Director of Safety, Northvale Cold Storage

**Subject:** Safety on your second shift

Hi John,

I noticed Northvale is hiring 12 forklift operators for a second shift, and that your careers page leads with a safety-first culture. New operators and a busier floor are when a good safety culture gets tested.

Ironbark Sense is forklift telematics with pedestrian-proximity alerts, impact detection and operator check-in. At Coldbrook Foods, one DC with 38 forklifts, recorded near-miss events fell 60% over six months. That's close to your fleet size.

We offer a free 30-day pilot on up to 10 trucks at one site. Would a 15-minute call next week be worth it to see if it fits?

Best,
[Name], Ironbark Safety

*(~115 words)*

---

## 3. Richard Roe, EHS Manager, Pellucid Beverages

**What I will do**
- **No email of any kind.** He unsubscribed on 11 Feb 2026. That includes "one-off" or personal-looking emails, and I'll make sure he's excluded from every sequence and list.
- **Make one phone call.** The CRM says phone is OK. I'll keep it short, say who I am, ask if it's a good time, and offer the free 30-day pilot as something to consider later.
- **Keep the OSHA citation out of my pitch.** If he raises it, I'll listen. I won't use it as a sales hook or imply anything about his incident.
- **Stop if he says no.** I'll log the outcome and any contact preference in the CRM.

**What I won't do**
- Use another channel to get around the unsubscribe, such as LinkedIn messages or a colleague's email.
- Make claims about what Sense would have prevented at his plant.

**Why:** The unsubscribe is a clear signal of how he wants to be contacted, and email compliance rules apply. Respecting it protects him, Ironbark and the relationship. A brief, respectful call is the one permitted route, and a recent citation means he may be busy and sensitive about the topic.

---

## 4. Note to Marketing

Team, I can't use "cuts forklift accidents by 60%. Guaranteed."

- The 60% is from one customer, Coldbrook Foods, and measures **recorded near-miss events** over 6 months. It isn't accidents. Impacts fell from 9 to 4 over 12 months.
- We have no approved guarantee, and a result from one site can't be promised for another.

Suggested replacement: "At Coldbrook Foods, recorded near-miss events fell 60% in six months." Please approve it or give me a better version. A free 30-day pilot lets prospects test the claim themselves.

*(~85 words)*

---

## 5. Rationale for angle and call to action

**Mary:** She asked a direct question and got no answer, so the first email answers it honestly (beta, about three customers live) before anything else. The follow-ups add the case study and a no-cost pilot that lets her test the integration. The third uses her Reno expansion and 200 hires. The CTA moves from a call, to a scoped pilot, to a call tied to her timeline.

**John:** The angle is his second-shift hiring and safety-first positioning, plus a Coldbrook case study at a similar fleet size. I deliberately did not mention the Tacoma fine, because Northvale Logistics is unrelated. The CTA is a low-friction 15-minute call, with the pilot as the offer.

**Richard:** Phone only, respecting the unsubscribe. The CTA is a brief conversation, with no pressure.
